name: Malformation Syndrome with Hamartosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Malformation Syndrome with Hamartosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple congenital malformations involving at least two organ systems
Identification of hamartomatous lesions confirmed by histopathology
Positive family history of similar malformations or hamartosis
Detection of pathogenic variants in genes associated with hamartosis syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple congenital malformations involving at least two organ systems plus histopathologically confirmed hamartomatous lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical and histopathological findings are primary.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically present from birth or early infancy
searchTerms: multiple benign growths present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital structural malformations affecting multiple organ systems
searchTerms: multiple organ malformations present from birth
congenital structural abnormalities in several systems

common.notes: Enlarged head circumference common in early childhood
Mild to moderate cognitive impairment observed
Patchy or diffuse skin pigmentation changes
Unequal limb length or body side differences

occasional.notes: Seizure types vary; may be focal or generalized
Includes septal defects or valve abnormalities
Hamartomatous polyps may cause bleeding or obstruction
Benign tumors affecting retina or iris

rare.notes: Includes thyroid or adrenal gland abnormalities

laboratory: Mild anemia or thrombocytopenia in some cases
imaging: MRI or CT showing multiple organ malformations
Ultrasound revealing renal cysts or gastrointestinal polyps
genetic: Pathogenic variants in PTEN, STK11, or other hamartosis-related genes (when identified)
other: Family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Hamartomatous polyps mainly in gastrointestinal tract

redFlags: Rapid growth or malignant transformation of hamartomatous lesions
Severe developmental delay or neurological regression
references: Orphanet: Malformation syndrome with hamartosis - ORPHA98196
